Archaeologists attempt to learn if this wreck is the famed Clotilda, and the physical evidence it could provide on the dark history of the slave trade.

snippet.title: New Discoveries Rewrite Maya History | Rise and Fall of the Maya MEGA Episode | National Geographic
snippet.description:
What actually happened to the ancient Maya? Mysteries unfold in this four episode Rise and Fall of the Maya Mega Episode compilation from National Geographic. Journey where the Maya lived in Mexico and Guatemala as archaeologists and historians uncover new evidence that rewrites what we know about this fascinating and mysterious ancient civilization. From the monumental discovery of a 3,000-year-old hidden megastructure to the puzzling, catastrophic collapse that forced millions to abandon their pyramid-filled cities, explore the origins of Maya power, secrets, and resilience in this documentary series. Featuring full episodes: 

Origins - 00:00 
What is Aguada Fénix? In June 2020, scientists discover Aguada Fénix, a monumental 3,000-year-old Maya structure. Uncover the hidden secrets of Aguada Fénix, the oldest monument built by the ancient Maya civilization, dating back to around 1000 BCE, that challenge everything we knew about the Maya's earliest days.

Civilization - 44:03 
New architectural and technological evidence unearthed in Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula transforms long-held ideas about how the Maya civilization grew into a superpower.

Collapse - 01:28:06
Why did the ancient Maya civilization collapse? Many cities were abandoned due to a complex combination of severe droughts, overpopulation, deforestation, and warfare. The exact series of events that lead the ancient Maya to abandon their pyramid-filled cities has long puzzled archaeologists. Now, new investigations in Mexico and Guatemala are exposing surprising evidence about why these great monuments were deserted. 

Resilience - 02:12:09
Archaeologists unearth new clues about the resurgence of the ancient Maya civilization and the devastating events that would ultimately lead them to abandon their cities for good. Investigations also reveal evidence of extreme resilience in the face of catastrophe. 

The Rise and Fall of the Maya | S1

Despite our ever-automated era, it’s proof that craft still draws in the kind of person who cares about all that came before them. They rely on a toolkit that works, Timberland gear that lasts as well as an appetite for change where it's needed, from new techniques to new philosophies and more.

snippet.description: The European Union banned battery cages for laying hens more than a decade ago. Now, activists are taking their campaign directly to supermarket shelves, hoping consumers will help drive change.

snippet.title: How Polygamist Cults Actually Work | How Crime Works | Insider
snippet.description:
Briell Decker is a former plural wife of Warren Jeffs, leader of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, or FLDS, a polygamist sect widely considered a cult.

Decker married Jeffs at 18 and spent eight years inside the group while it was being investigated by several law enforcement agencies. Decker explains how the FLDS manipulated its members, including through arranged marriages, financial control, isolation, and the use of religious authority to enforce obedience. She also describes her multiple escape attempts and the pressure the church used to keep members from leaving.

Warren Jeffs was arrested in 2006 and, in 2011, was sentenced to life in prison plus 20 years for sexually assaulting underage girls.

Decker now works with people leaving polygamist communities as founder of the Short Creek Dream Center. She appeared in the HBO Max/Discovery+ documentary "Prisoner of the Prophet."

If you are a survivor of sexual assault, you can call the National Sexual Assault Hotline (1-800-656-4673) or visit its website to receive confidential support.

snippet.title: XPLOSION: Inside South Africa’s Underground Taxi Raves
snippet.description:
In 1980s South Africa during Apartheid, racist “influx control” laws made it almost impossible for black taxi drivers to earn a living. They upgraded their sedans to minibuses and worked illegally, providing vital transport for their communities. The end of Apartheid created a new problem, as the underground taxi network was replaced by a cutthroat system where corruption thrived and competition over routes turned brutally violent. Intimidation and targeted killings became commonplace.

Deaths in the “Taxi Wars” peaked in the late 90s, but the industry remains highly dangerous. Even now, most assassinations in South Africa are related to taxi violence. And while most drivers are armed with some kind of weapon, most are just men trying to feed their families.

For the young and the bored, the taxis sometimes perform a different function, providing a confined space with a dance floor the size of a phone box where they can listen to gqom at deafening volume and take umgwinyo: a synthetic drug, like ecstasy, that they use to summon the spirits of the dead.

The events, called Umqhumo (which translates as “explosion”), are held in secret locations where Durban’s humid jungle sprawl meets the Indian Ocean. Taxis line up beside one another in formation, each run by a different team that produces its own music for the night, with a dedicated MC and loyal followers. VICE rode along with Team Orange, hosted by producer Papa J and lead “party guy” Junior Mike.

6 - Manicured Reputation
Alliauna Green, better known as rapper Tan DaGod, was celebrating the grand opening of an Oakland beauty supply store when everything took a sudden and terrible turn. What was supposed to be a casual meet-and-greet with fans ended in chaos, leaving Green unalive and another person injured. 

5 - Firearm Safety
Tonika Miller from Indianapolis, Indiana, was sentenced to just one year behind bars after striking Dashawn Roscoe, the father of her two children, with a firearm, causing it to discharge during an argument. The incident, which took place back in 2022, started as an ill-advised late-night trip to a playground for an adult rendezvous but quickly wound up in a tragic confrontation.

4 - His Last Words
Brittany Holbrook from Key West, Florida, was convicted of offing her boyfriend, Tyler Nulisch, after a chaotic night in their shared home. She claimed the incident was self-defense, but the evidence—and Nulisch’s final words—told a very different story.

3 - Wrong Crowds
Jackson Gilmour from Rye, Australia, had been keeping different company lately, and it may have put him on a dangerous path. One moment, he was asleep in his home, and the next thing he knew, he was in a confrontation with intruders—19-year-old Charlyze Hayter, Jarod Smit, and an unidentified 28-year-old man. 

2 - The Untrusting Dad 
Richard Jones from the UK, was sentenced to life in prison for offing his son’s girlfriend, Sophie Evans, in what he claimed was a moment of paranoia. But instead of reacting with shock or remorse after the crime, he casually went to a bakery to pick up a custard slice and a tuna roll.Watch this video to learn all about the saddest crimes!

1 - Unhinged
Chelsea Cook, a former high school teacher from Utah, received a sentence of 34 years to life for taking the life of Lisa Vilate Williams. The incident unfolded back in 2018 when Cook entered her ex-husband’s apartment and carried out the act in front of her 3-year-old twins.

snippet.title: We Asked a CIA Spy 27 Tough Questions | Honesty Box
snippet.description:
Former CIA officer Jason Hanson answers the internet’s biggest questions in this episode of Honesty Box.

Jason explains how people really get into the CIA, what surveillance and counter-surveillance actually look like, how intelligence officers recruit sources, and why the world of espionage is often very different from what we see in films.

He also discusses sleeper agents, public Wi-Fi, phone security, spy tactics, foreign intelligence, government secrecy, and what life inside the CIA can do to your personal life.

This episode contains discussions of espionage, surveillance, violence, organised crime, terrorism, government agencies and sensitive real-world events that some viewers may find distressing.

Thank you to Jason Hanson for taking part in this episode of Honesty Box. You can find out more about his work at: 
@JasonHansonSpyBriefing
https://spybriefing.com/
